tests.reason: B3 ships dark: VITANA_INDEX_DUAL_COMPUTE_ENABLED and HEALTH_FEATURES_SOURCE are unset everywhere, both are forced off when VITANA_ENV=staging (staging shares the production database), the switch also needs HEALTH_FEATURES_CUTOVER_DATE and the writers' own dual-write flags, and vitana_index_dual_compute plus the projection functions are Aurora-only and absent from the shared Supabase project. So on staging the daily recompute, every health writer, the D6a bridge and W-sql behave exactly as before and the Index members see cannot change. The read-only GETs above prove the build is live and the new admin route is mounted behind its auth gate (a non-admin 403 needs a signed-in session, which this harness does not create; it is proven in admin-dual-compute-route.test.ts). The daily-recompute route is a write path and is never called on staging. Jest proves the rest: the final step's order, index-only users, budget, staging/flag no-op and untouched batch fields (daily-recompute-dual-compute.test.ts); every diff_class, R_dev, the report's aggregates-only payload and the Stage 1/2 criteria (index-dual-compute.test.ts); the switch, target 'live' and the fatal synchronous cutover path (cutover.test.ts); every writer byte-identical in every switch-off state, and the derived_device / derived behaviour at each call site (cutover-writers.test.ts); the bridge's shadow mode (vtid-05089); the SQL key classes, STABLE functions and workflow path triggers (vtid-05163 migration test). The functional drift guard, routing, STABLE, grants, erasure, the rollback fix-up and the placement guard run on a throwaway Postgres in scripts/ci/sql-tests/run-index-dual-compute-test.sh (CI SQL-INDEX-DUAL-COMPUTE.yml; outputs/sql-index-dual-compute.txt).
